papers.title: A Coulomb Particle Model for Learning Kernel Attention in Transformers

summary.tldr: A particle-based method learns feature distributions for kernel machines by optimizing kernel-target alignment with Riesz/Coulomb repulsive potential, yielding task-adaptive random features for linearized Transformer attention.
key_points: The method learns feature distributions by optimizing kernel-target alignment while regularizing particles with a Riesz/Coulomb repulsive potential.
The resulting Hamiltonian provides diverse, task-adaptive random features and has a mean-field description via a McKean--Vlasov equation.
The approach is instantiated in linearized Transformer attention by learning positive random-feature maps in a first alignment phase.
After freezing the kernel, the remaining network parameters are trained with cross-entropy.

Experiments show improved accuracy, calibration, and robustness for learned kernelized attention on synthetic classification and sentence-level benchmarks, maintaining linear-attention inference complexity.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a way to improve the performance of linearized Transformer attention by learning task-adaptive random features, potentially enhancing accuracy and robustness without increasing inference complexity.

papers.title: TriShieldRAG: A Three-Ring Defense-in-Depth Framework Against Knowledge Corruption in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: TriShieldRAG is a three-stage defense framework that reduces knowledge corruption attack success in RAG systems from 91% to 13% by screening ingested documents, re-ranking retrieved sets, and using cross-LLM consensus.
key_points: TriShieldRAG implements three defense rings: Ingest Guard (screens documents for poisoning signatures), Retrieval Scorer (re-ranks retrieved documents by provenance and consistency-weighted trust), and Cross-LLM Consensus (polls Claude, Mistral Small, Llama 3.2, allows bounded re-retrieval on disagreement).
The framework reduces attack success rate from 91% to 13% against the PoisonedRAG non-adaptive attacker on a 5,000-document Wikipedia knowledge base with 10 target questions.
Previous single-stage defenses (perplexity filtering, query paraphrasing, knowledge-base expansion) left attack success rates at 30% or higher.
Rings 2 and 3 operate under assumptions of minority poison and explicit provenance tagging.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework significantly improves the trustworthiness of RAG systems by mitigating knowledge corruption attacks, making them more reliable for sensitive or dynamic information.

papers.title: Kalypso: Relational LLM Serving

summary.tldr: Kalypso introduces relational LLM serving, an abstraction that makes LLM serving aware of semantic query structure, enabling pipelined execution and KV-cache reuse for improved performance.
key_points: Kalypso reuses KV-cache state across pipelined semantic operators, avoiding recomputation.
It features an adaptive, memory-aware scheduling algorithm that couples pipelined execution with GPU memory pressure management.
The scheduler continuously adjusts memory allocations to balance upstream parallelism, downstream progress, and GPU utilization.
Kalypso achieves speedups up to 4.57x over request-centric LLM serving baselines across diverse workloads.
summary.why_it_matters: Query-aware LLM serving substantially improves the efficiency of semantic query execution by optimizing resource utilization.

papers.title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks

summary.tldr: ACM is a framework for agentic context management that uses purpose-built context editing tools for lossless context management, inspired by human memory, to autonomously compress and offload context.
key_points: ACM equips agents with purpose-built context editing tools for lossless context management.
The agent autonomously decides when to compress context, offloads discarded content to external memory, and queries it on demand.
A post-training pipeline constructs high-quality demonstrations for context management, improving performance on agentic search and coding tasks.
Effective context management reduces peak token pressure, enables extended explorations, and yields more consistent solutions.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework addresses the limitations of existing context compression methods by providing a more dynamic and lossless approach to managing context in long-horizon agentic tasks.

papers.title: Asymmetric Collapse in Model Merging: When Refusal Over- writes Recognition

summary.tldr: Model merging methods applied to Gemma-3-1B-IT fine-tunes for safety tasks show asymmetric collapse, with jailbreak refusal rates retained (81-85%) while classification accuracy significantly drops (to 12.9%).
key_points: Two Gemma-3-1B-IT fine-tunes were created for CARES harm-level classification and WildJailbreak adversarial refusal.
Merging methods (Linear, SLERP, TIES, DARE-TIES) resulted in merged models retaining 81-85% jailbreak refusal rates.
Classification accuracy in merged models dropped to at most 12.9%.
Task vectors for the two objectives were nearly orthogonal (cosine similarity 0.011), indicating non-opposing directions.
Refusal fine-tune induced consistently larger per-layer task-vector magnitudes, biasing magnitude-sensitive merging methods towards refusal.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard model merging can lead to safety recognition collapsing into broad refusal when task vector scales differ, impacting the preservation of specific safety behaviors.

papers.title: A Frozen 12B Beats Frontier Models on Verified Work: 100% Accuracy, 0 Tokens, Bit-Exact, Forever

summary.tldr: A frozen 12B model, augmented with a verified memory, achieves 100% accuracy on solved problem families with zero generation tokens, outperforming frontier models on these specific tasks.
key_points: A frozen 12B model, coupled with a persistent memory of verified solutions, achieves 100% accuracy across 180 instances spanning nine problem families with zero generation tokens.
The system demonstrates 88/88 consistency-gated acceptances for open-ended reasoning with machine-checked formal proof and 77/80 reasoning-method transfer.
Memory selection takes 1.4 microseconds, with full reuse completing in 6-23 ms at 36 mWh.
The memory functions as a 6,000,000-token movable context window on a single 46 GB GPU, exceeding vLLM (30,399 tokens) and SGLang (32,000 tokens) capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a method for achieving deterministic, bit-exact, and token-free answers for verified problem families, providing a cost-effective alternative to continuous retraining and fresh generation passes by frontier models.

papers.title: How Context Attribution Handles What the Model Already Knows

summary.tldr: New research introduces an evaluation protocol and benchmark dataset to assess context attribution methods in LLMs, revealing their unfaithfulness when input context overlaps with model training data.
key_points: Context attribution methods fail to disentangle in-context from in-weight contributions when context overlaps with training data, leading to unreliable scores.

A new evaluation protocol is introduced, featuring four metrics: base-model context attribution score (BCS), cross-model context attribution consistency (CAC), attribution preservation score (APS), and source separation precision (SSP).
A benchmark dataset, WMDP-Cyber++, with ground-truth provenance labels, is developed to systematically assess attribution under in-weight overlap.
Experiments with four established context attribution methods demonstrate unfaithful attribution when knowledge from the context also exists in the model's weights.
Adapted methods for source separation (in-weight vs. in-context learning) are shown to be incapable of disentanglement based on contributive scores.
summary.why_it_matters: The inability of current context attribution methods to distinguish between in-context and in-weight contributions limits their reliability for understanding LLM behavior and ensuring responsible AI development.

papers.title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement

summary.tldr: RLSVR extends RLVR to open-ended tasks by transforming them into verifiable proxy environments, generating self-verifiable reward signals for LLM self-improvement.
key_points: RLSVR transforms open-ended tasks into verifiable proxy environments, where internal rules and interaction outcomes automatically generate reward signals.
SpyRL instantiates RLSVR using a multi-agent self-play environment inspired by 'Who Is the Spy?', where agents receive asymmetric information and vote to identify a predetermined spy.
Voting outcomes in SpyRL provide fully verifiable rewards because the spy's identity is known, and successful identification correlates with output quality.
Experiments show SpyRL outperforms existing self-improvement methods on non-verifiable tasks (text summarization, creative writing) and improves verifiable reasoning tasks (mathematical reasoning).
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables scalable RLVR-based self-improvement for LLMs in open-ended domains, reducing reliance on human preferences or costly LLM-based judges.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Cooperate with Inference-Time Controllers

summary.tldr: CALM is a post-training framework that integrates diverse inference-time controllers into the training loop, improving generalization across various LLM workflows.
key_points: CALM formulates controller-aware post-training as multi-task reinforcement learning over controller-induced interaction protocols.
Controllers are defined as compositions of reusable local reasoning modules.
The framework uses a module-level decomposition of mixed-controller training with a turn-level GRPO objective.
Evaluation shows improved generalization on held-out controller compositions and broader controller shifts compared to single-controller optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach addresses the training-deployment mismatch in LLMs, enabling better transferability to new and diverse inference-time workflows.

papers.title: Auditing Alignment Controllability in LLMs via Political Axes

summary.tldr: This study introduces a dispersion-first stress test for LLM political alignment, demonstrating that prompt-based steering accounts for 88-93% of response variance, significantly more than model identity.
key_points: Contextual framing via system prompts explains 88-93% of variance on economic and society axes in LLM responses, while model identity accounts for less than 3%.
The study tested 7 leading LLMs (GPT-5, Claude, Grok, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen) across 12 ideological personas, 70 Political Compass items, and ten replicates, generating 63,700 responses.
Models exhibit differential steerability: some shift more, and some reach saturation under extreme framings.
Prior conflicting directional-steering audit results are resolved by recognizing non-centered baselines, indicating a geometric rather than differential compliance effect.
Political-coordinate audits should include steerability metrics such as dispersion, symmetry, saturation, and refusal floors.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding LLM steerability is crucial for developing robust alignment audits that account for dynamic, prompt-induced shifts in political responses rather than static baselines.

papers.title: Ranked by Position: Order Sensitivity as an Exploitable Attack Surface in LLM Listwise Recommenders

summary.tldr: LLM listwise rerankers exhibit position bias, allowing attackers to promote label-0 items into top-k recommendations by reordering candidates, quantified by promo@k, and mitigated by regularization or architectural invariance.
key_points: Position bias in LLM listwise rerankers creates an attack surface where reordering candidates promotes label-0 items into top-k rankings.
The promo@k metric quantifies this vulnerability; promo@5 reached up to 0.57 on MovieLens, Amazon Books, and Amazon Fashion with 50 orderings.
Permutation stability predicts vulnerability without requiring attack execution.
A bidirectional T5 encoder scorer reduces exposure, but permutation-consistency regularization and architectural invariance are effective mitigation strategies.
Pointwise scoring avoids position bias but degrades ranking quality.
summary.why_it_matters: Input candidate order in listwise LLM reranking is a security-relevant attack vector that can be exploited to manipulate recommendations.

papers.title: The Intruder Threshold: A Spectral Law for LoRA Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: A new spectral law predicts the emergence of intruder dimensions in LoRA fine-tuning, which cause catastrophic forgetting, with high accuracy across diverse Transformer models.
key_points: The derived per-layer critical update strength $s^\ast=\bar\theta/(\gamma\sigma_1(BA))$ predicts intruder dimension appearance from the measured spectrum of $W$ alone.

The law localized the empirical threshold within a factor of two on 82% of layers and separated intruder-bearing from intruder-free layers with a mean AUC of 0.89 across 18 adapters and 9,840 layer scans.
Full fine-tuning disperses its update below the threshold of every layer, explaining the asymmetry with LoRA.
A spike-budget rule, derived from thresholds, reduces forgetting by 62% on the most fragile model without task cost, requiring one SVD and no validation sweeps.
summary.why_it_matters: This theory provides a method to predict and mitigate catastrophic forgetting in LoRA fine-tuning, improving model stability and efficiency.

papers.title: The Mirage of LLM Guardrails: A Case Study in AI-Assisted Medical Note Manipulation

summary.tldr: This paper empirically investigates the robustness of LLM guardrails against AI-assisted medical note manipulation, revealing substantial weaknesses and inconsistencies in commercial LLMs.
key_points: A reproducible manipulation pipeline was developed to customize seed medical note templates using commercial LLMs by substituting patient names, provider identities, dates, and medical conditions.
Systematic evaluation showed low refusal rates for several commercial LLM families against medical note manipulation queries.
Automated and human annotation metrics assessed the correctness of requested manipulations.
User studies found that the best manipulated medical notes were visually indistinguishable from original documents to human raters.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings highlight critical vulnerabilities in LLM guardrails, posing risks for AI safety and ethical deployment in healthcare.

papers.title: Do LLMs Know Their Vulnerable Scenarios?

summary.tldr: This work introduces Concept2Scenario, a concept-based attribution framework that identifies internal scenario directions in LLMs, causally linking them to reduced refusal scores and enabling discovery of vulnerable scenarios that bypass safety safeguards.
key_points: Scenario-wrapped prompts activate internal scenario directions that causally steer LLMs to reduce refusal scores.
Concept2Scenario uses a sparse autoencoder to instantiate a broad concept space, attributes refusal suppression to individual concepts, and translates these into natural-language scenarios.
The framework identifies synergistic scenario combinations through interaction attribution, outperforming individual constituents and enabling iterative attacks.
Discovered scenarios improve average attack success rates by up to 18.2 percentage points across three open-source models, two safety benchmarks, and six black-box jailbreak methods.
Identified scenario-level refusal vulnerabilities transfer to GPT-5, Claude-Haiku-4.5, and Gemini-3-Flash, indicating cross-model family commonality.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a mechanistic understanding and a systematic approach to discover and exploit LLM safety vulnerabilities, improving red-teaming and potentially informing more robust safety alignment.

papers.title: Isolated but Exposed: Persistence-Based Memory Extraction Attack on LLM Agents

summary.tldr: SPORE is the first memory extraction attack on LLM agents that exploits the tool interface to exfiltrate private long-term memory despite user-level isolation.
key_points: SPORE decouples adversarial commands from retrieval anchors by persisting the command in short-term memory and emitting semantically pure anchors in tool responses.
The attack uses a geometric coverage optimization over the embedding space to systematically steer anchors toward unexplored memory regions, restoring retrieval precision.
SPORE persists reactivation payloads in memory to automatically resume extraction within and across sessions, bypassing tool-call limits and requiring no additional user triggers.
SPORE achieves an 80.0% record extraction rate with unlimited triggers and 47.0% with only 20 triggers.
summary.why_it_matters: Memory isolation alone is insufficient to protect privacy-sensitive user data in LLM agents, necessitating a reevaluation of tool-side trust boundaries.

papers.title: Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in recommendation systems

summary.tldr: This paper introduces Dual-purpose Semantic IDs, using hierarchical quantization to condense continuous embeddings into discrete tokens for both collaborative identity and on-the-fly content reconstruction, achieving LLM-level I/O efficiency in recommendation systems.
key_points: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs condense continuous embeddings into discrete tokens via hierarchical quantization.
Semantic IDs serve as Collaborative Identity for user-item interaction modeling through a learnable embedding table.
Semantic IDs enable Content Reconstruction using a lightweight Semantic Decoder for on-the-fly embedding approximation.
This method replaces massive vector storage with on-demand reconstruction, reducing system overhead and data footprints.
The framework was successfully deployed in production-scale ranking and retrieval systems at a major video sharing platform.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach addresses the "Memory Wall" bottleneck in large-scale recommendation systems by significantly improving I/O efficiency and reducing storage requirements.

papers.title: A Few Words Go a Long Way: Language Guided Robot Policy Synthesis

summary.tldr: ARCHITECT is a framework for robot policy acquisition that uses LLM coding agents to synthesize modular robot programs, outperforming state-of-the-art VLA models on complex, long-horizon tasks.
key_points: ARCHITECT treats robot policy acquisition as an interactive program synthesis task, leveraging LLM coding agents to synthesize modular robot programs.
The framework utilizes a suite of perception and control tools, allowing users to isolate failures and localize feedback at the required abstraction level.
A human supervisor provides natural language corrections grounded in program execution traces, which are distilled into a persistent skill library for long-term in-context learning.

In benchmark evaluations on a Franka Panda robot, ARCHITECT outperformed state-of-the-art VLA models and program synthesis baselines on complex tasks like articulated object manipulation and cloth folding.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a steerable and data-efficient alternative to black-box robot learning, enabling transfer to novel tasks with decreasing human intervention.

papers.title: WISERouter: LLM Routing with Workload Budget Constraint

summary.tldr: WISERouter (WR) is a new LLM routing framework that addresses budget constraints and data collection challenges by formulating routing as a constrained contextual multi-armed bandit problem, supporting both offline and online learning.
key_points: WISERouter (WR) formulates LLM routing as a constrained contextual multi-armed bandit problem to balance utility and budget.
WR supports offline learning from historical interactions and online learning with exploration, addressing the need for dense, supervised datasets.
WR-Online achieves a sublinear regret bound of O(sqrt(T)) over a time horizon T.

Empirical results on RouterBench and SWE-Bench show WR-Offline outperforms baselines under fixed budgets and adheres to constraints, while WR-Online achieves comparable performance with less exploration data.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework allows for more efficient and cost-effective deployment of LLMs by optimizing model selection under budget constraints without extensive data collection.

papers.title: E-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Step Tool-Use Agents in Real-World Product Scenarios

summary.tldr: E-Bench is a new synthetic benchmark for multi-step tool-use agents, featuring 323 state-changing tasks across three product domains, designed to evaluate agents' ability to discover hidden data and compose multiple tool calls.
key_points: E-Bench includes 323 state-changing tasks across Honor of Kings, QQ Music, and Tencent Meeting product domains.
The benchmark decouples environment synthesis from task synthesis, using graph-guided database filling for environments and generator-solver asymmetry for tasks.
Tasks require agents to address both an information gap and a tool gap, necessitating discovery of hidden data and composition of multiple tool calls.
Outcomes are deterministically graded by database-state diffs.
Benchmarking 11 LLMs showed Pass^3 scores below 60% for the strongest models, and below 70% even with code execution in E-Bench-Code.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark highlights that multi-step tool use remains a significant challenge for current LLMs, even with advanced capabilities like code execution.

papers.title: The Illusion of Secure LLM Code: Closing the Security Gap via Iterative Reprompting

summary.tldr: Iterative reprompting, forcing LLMs into a self-auditing loop, is strictly required to generate secure authentication code, as single-shot prompts consistently omit critical protections.
key_points: Five AI coding assistants were evaluated for authentication system security using static analysis and dynamic penetration testing against NIST SP 800-63B guidelines.
Code from basic or generically secure prompts lacked brute-force resistance, session management, and robust password handling.
Single-shot NIST context improved compliance but was structurally inadequate for comprehensive security.
Iterative reprompting, a contextual self-auditing loop, was necessary to achieve a defense-in-depth security architecture.
summary.why_it_matters: Enterprise deployments of AI coding assistants must adopt continuous, standards-driven verification pipelines instead of single-shot prompt engineering to ensure application security.

papers.title: Offline-Online Curriculum RL for Multimodal Reasoning

summary.tldr: O^2-CritiCuRL is a curriculum reinforcement learning framework that uses an iterative offline-online paradigm to identify and focus on critical reasoning steps in multimodal LLMs, improving interpretability and performance.
key_points: The offline stage uses multi-rollout analysis on step-annotated trajectories to estimate step-level importance, distilling critical steps and filtering redundant ones.
The online stage employs progressive step-level reinforcement learning, where truncated chains guide the model to infer missing steps and refine reasoning.
The method addresses the challenge of distinguishing decisive from redundant steps in step-level supervision for multimodal reasoning.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance and superior training/inference efficiency on multimodal reasoning benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enhances the interpretability and reliability of multimodal large language models by ensuring faithful reasoning rather than reliance on spurious shortcuts.

papers.title: Focus Is All You Need: Adaptive Goal-aware Attention Orchestration for Multi-Agent Graph Systems

summary.tldr: AGAO introduces Attention Orchestration for multi-agent graph systems, dynamically allocating computational focus based on user goals, graph dependencies, and resource constraints to improve task effectiveness and efficiency.
key_points: AGAO extends Transformer-style attention to workflow-level agent coordination in multi-agent graph systems.
The framework comprises three components: goal-aware attention (semantic relevance), topology-aware attention (structural dependencies), and resource-aware attention (budget/priority allocation).
AGAO dynamically estimates agent importance to transform static agent graphs into adaptive systems focusing on goal-critical reasoning paths.
Experiments demonstrate AGAO improves task effectiveness while reducing computation, latency, and token consumption compared to existing graph-based execution strategies.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more scalable and intelligent multi-agent systems by optimizing resource allocation and computational focus.

papers.title: SpecAHD: Localize to Specialize for Automated Heuristic Design in Large-Scale Routing Problems

summary.tldr: SpecAHD introduces a bilevel framework for automated heuristic design in large-scale routing, specializing heuristics for localized repair regions to improve performance.
key_points: SpecAHD is a coupled bilevel framework for within-instance specialization in large-scale routing problems.
The upper-level search identifies bounded repair regions, while the lower-level evolves heuristics for these induced repair tasks.
The lower-level objective is monotone submodular for a fixed upper-level program and candidate pool, enabling greedy repertoire selection with a (1-1/e) approximation guarantee.
SpecAHD reduces held-out objective cost by up to 57.7% compared to the strongest AHD baseline across four routing problems and multiple LLM backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly improves the performance of automated heuristic design in complex routing problems by adapting heuristics to specific problem sub-regions.

papers.title: CALMRec: Causally Aligned Language Memory for Long-Horizon Recommendation

summary.tldr: CALMRec is a model-agnostic framework for long-horizon recommendation that uses a frozen multimodal language model to create semantic atoms and maintains separate short-term, long-term, and exposure memories.
key_points: Uses a frozen multimodal language model to convert item content and feedback into evidence-grounded semantic atoms.
Maintains separate short-term, long-term, and exposure memories to differentiate enduring preferences, transient intent, and exposure-induced behavior.
Applies propensity-weighted updates to reduce policy-induced exposure bias and uses a conservative offline critic for reranking to achieve delayed satisfaction under a behavior-support constraint.
Improves discounted long-term value over the strongest alternative by 6.1% (e-commerce), 7.6% (news), and 6.7% (short-video) across ten seeds.
Ablation studies show significant value drops after removing propensity correction (0.739 +/- 0.191) or conservative support regularization (0.523 +/- 0.234).
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a robust approach to mitigate feedback loops and exposure bias in recommender systems, leading to more accurate and satisfying long-term user experiences.

papers.title: HVM-GraphRAG: Holistic-View Multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Complex Document

summary.tldr: HVM-GraphRAG introduces a holistic-view multimodal GraphRAG framework for complex document QA, improving evidence indexing and retrieval efficiency by using concept-level graphs and direct access to multimodal chunks.
key_points: HVM-GraphRAG employs a holistic view to guide graph construction, reducing noisy updates and building reliable indices between concept-level graph nodes and supporting multimodal chunks.
Retrieval in HVM-GraphRAG searches a compact concept-level graph and directly accesses supporting evidence via indices, avoiding costly traversal over dense entity-level graphs.
After retrieval, HVM-GraphRAG reorganizes chunks into modality-specific groups to enhance integration of heterogeneous evidence by the answering model.
Experiments show HVM-GraphRAG achieves superior answer performance and substantially improves online retrieval efficiency compared to graph-based baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more efficient and accurate approach to question answering over complex, multimodal documents, addressing limitations of existing GraphRAG techniques.

vendors.title: An Inside Look at the Relay Market Powering Token Resellers and Fraud

summary.tldr: A market exists for reselling LLM tokens at a discount, primarily in China, using pooled API keys obtained through various exploits, raising concerns about LLM application abuse.
key_points: Token resellers offer discounted LLM access by pooling API keys from free trials, unprotected support bots, stolen credit cards, or chargeback attacks.
The primary software used for these proxy services is open-source, specifically "one-api" and its fork "new-api", which are legitimate API proxy products.
Buyers seek cheap tokens, geo-restriction avoidance, and data for model distillation.
The market is largely concentrated in China, as indicated by the principal source being a Chinese-language forum thread.
summary.why_it_matters: The existence of this market increases the risk of abuse for publicly exposed LLM-driven applications, necessitating better API key capping mechanisms from LLM vendors.
